content:
- Overestimate prices after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot post-peak sentiment (e.g., +0.33 sentiment → forecast peaks then drops).
- Underestimate downward trends when sentiment is negative or neutral; model fails to recognize mean reversion in 30d horizon.
- Lag in correction: model often delays downward adjustment, especially after negative sentiment (e.g., -0.20 → forecast still high for 2–3 days).
- Overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; model overweights sentiment spikes (e.g., 0.33 → forecast jumps, then fails to correct).
- 30d horizon underestimates volatility in early days; model assumes smoother decay than actual sharp drops (e.g., 76.20 → 68.53 in 10 days).
- When sentiment is flat (0.00), model tends to overfit recent history, ignoring true mean reversion.
- Avoid extrapolating recent highs as sustainable; model often assumes continuation of recent trend, even when sentiment suggests reversal.
